P1.evidence: Setter was acknowledged but the notes were never read back so the prospect could feel seen — only 'You spoke with Kim, I think, right?... He gave you me some notes, so I've kind of got a head start on you.' The frame was three-part rather than four: 'I just want to get a good idea of where you're at, build out what it is that you want, and then if there's alignment, we can talk about the coaching and stuff, and if not, that's fine as well' — no 'what's in the way' and no 'what you need'. Agreement was sought and given ('Alrighty?' / 'Cool. No problem.'). The open question was asked properly: 'What was it that you were hoping that we could potentially help you out with, man?'

P2.evidence: The open question triggered an eleven-minute uninterrupted monologue and the rep then treated it as the baseline, asking almost nothing. No age, height or weight on a body-composition call. Work was never asked — the sales-lead role, the seven-day week and the shift from on-feet to desk-bound all arrived unprompted. Health conditions were never asked; the polytrauma was volunteered. Pain was the one genuine hit: 'Whereabouts do you have pain?' followed by 'Is that like a big priority, the getting out of the pain?' Training capacity was asked forward-looking ('would you be able to make 30 minutes a day four days a week') rather than establishing actual days trained. Diet was never asked at all — the prospect had to raise his own vegetarianism twice before it was addressed. No sleep, no energy, no results from current training.

P3.evidence: The strongest discovery in the call. Surface goal asked cleanly — 'if we were to look six months down the line, what is it that you're... What does it all look like for you? What's the outcome?' — producing lean, cut, muscle without bulk. The deep question was then asked properly and is the best single move on the tape: 'let's say six months down the line you are where you want to be... what actually changes for you?', which produced 'a whole lifestyle change, a different approach on life' and 'pretty much becoming a new, a new person'. 'I'm curious, why now?' served as a partial bridge and surfaced the workhorse admission. But the rep supplied the identity language himself ('the best version of you, in a way') instead of driving the prospect to it, never asked who else it impacts — the prospect volunteered friends and family unprompted — and never ran the reflect-back. Nothing physical-he-cannot-do-now was asked despite baseball, basketball and marathons all being on the table.

P4.evidence: Not a single past-attempts question was asked. The prospect handed the whole phase over unprompted — searching online for programmes, starting one, stopping, 'not having that end goal at the end of the day', and wanting the accountability he had with his physical therapist. Under the rule that the script credits asking rather than luck, that is a miss on P4a through P4d. The rep did engage the gap once it was on the table: 'Do you feel like you have enough of an end goal at this point to make sure you stick to it?', and ran a decent structural variant of P4f in the Ferrari frame — 'we can 100% be the Ferrari to get you around the racetrack. But you've still got to turn the key and turn the wheel and put your foot on the pedal.'

P5.evidence: No consequence frame was built. No two-year question, no 'is that something you're willing to settle for', no 'why not'. The line in the sand was asked and answered well — 'Do you feel like you're ready to be courageous and really go for it? And really go for the change?' / 'Yeah, man. definitely feel like it's, I got it in me.' The waste here is large: the prospect had already supplied the raw material himself, describing going from 33,000 steps a day to being out of breath on a couple of flights of stairs and 'I think I've let myself go because of that'. Turning that into a cost of inaction would have taken one question and it was never asked.

P6.evidence: The best-run phase in the batch so far and correctly sequenced. Before naming any number the rep stopped and asked: 'I've got one question for you, then we'll kind of go through the numbers... do you feel like with everything we've gone through, do you feel like we can get you where you want to go? Because that's the most important thing, right?' He got an unambiguous yes with reasons attached — the tailored plan and the form-feedback loop — and only then moved to price. The all-in question was not asked in its own right beforehand; the nearest equivalent came later inside the money objection as 'Is there anything else that's holding you back, or is it just that?', which is the isolation move doing double duty.

P11.evidence: Payment was collected on the call, not deferred to a link: the rep screen-shared Stripe, took the email and began entering the charge after the prospect said 'Let's do it dude.' The Trevor onboarding call was described and offered for the next day ('we can do tomorrow', 'get you all booked in for tomorrow with Trevor') but no booking was actually completed on the recording. No agreement email was mentioned and nothing was signed on the call. No welcome email, no Skool community link, no onboarding questionnaire. Caveat recorded honestly: the recording was deliberately stopped at the point of payment, so steps 2 to 4 may have been run off-tape — but they are not evidenced, and the score reflects what is demonstrable.

objection_plays.detail: Triggered twice — the expectation gap ('I was not expecting 6k... I was expecting someone, I know above 3k easy') and then real affordability ('right now, like I owe some things that I got to pay off'). The isolation move ran, correctly and twice: 'do you feel like we can actually help you money aside? That's the most important bit, right?' and 'Is there anything else that's holding you back, or is it just that?' The break-it-up move ran: 'we can figure it out... We can break it up if we need to.' A partial cash-on-hand probe ran: 'when it comes to the 6k, like, do you have it?' Not run: the should-I-versus-how frame, the permission question for an open financial conversation, monthly surplus after bills, number of credit cards, available credit per card, used versus available, and investments. The rep improvised past the script instead — asking for a credit score and offering Klarna, neither of which is in the play. Net: the isolation half was executed well, the financial-picture half was almost entirely skipped, and the gap was filled with third-party consumer credit.

Clinical fit — the most serious instance in this batch and there is no scripted path for it. The prospect disclosed being struck by a car at 30+ mph, thrown 20+ feet, a year on crutches and a cane, a second collision two years ago, and current active left-sided neck, shoulder and upper-back pain with contralateral compensation. The rep's entire handling was 'you've probably got some imbalances, dude, but it's fine. We'll fix it.' He then described the first workout as 'swings, into snatches, into push-ups as a circuit'. Nothing in the playbook prompts a clearance question, so the rep had nothing to reach for — but he also went further than silence and affirmatively reassured. This is the known script gap producing its worst-case output.

Product-feature objection with no scripted play. The prospect asked for live coaching contact twice, explicitly modelled on his physiotherapist relationship — 'if we have like actual face-to-face calls... that would also help out a lot' and then 'how would that take place, like through Zoom calls?' The rep answered honestly that the product has none ('we don't do any calls... it ended up just being a waste of time') and reframed to 24/7 asynchronous support, which is a defensible reframe. He then undercut it with an off-menu personal commitment — 'I would jump on with you. I've done it for people before where I've said I'll jump on with you once a month' — which resolves the objection by promising something outside the product.

notes: Two very different halves. Phase 6 was textbook and correctly sequenced — belief question asked and answered before a number was ever spoken — and phase 3 got to genuine identity-level motivation with one excellent question. Everything underneath was skipped: the eleven-minute opening monologue was treated as a substitute for baseline and past-attempts, so no age, height, weight, diet, sleep or energy was ever taken, and the consequence frame was left unbuilt on a call that had handed the rep perfect material for it. The coaching priority is not the close, which worked; it is that this rep converts on rapport and belief while flying blind on the physical facts — and on this call the physical facts were a polytrauma patient with active spinal and shoulder pain being routed toward snatches.
